correctness.rationale: Gaussian normalization and the orthogonal splitting give the exact kernel. The harmonic minimum principle plus strict boundary derivative yield the optimal log(2) contact and equality conditions. Three exhaustive parameter ranges establish the least zero is simple, while its implicit derivative is strictly negative. Taylor expansion at the unique antipodal contact gives the square-root coefficient; the exponential first-root bound yields the two-term far-field chord expansion. All quantifiers and limits are explicit; numerical checks are supplementary only.

value.rationale: The sharp first orthogonality radius, the complete smooth first-angular-branch law, and its square-root/inverse-radius regimes are natural quantitative geometric invariants of a reproducing-kernel Hilbert space. The far-field result establishes the substantive boundary phenomenon that orthogonal evaluation vectors can be arbitrarily close in Euclidean distance, in sharp contrast to holomorphic Fock space; it informs conditioning and sampling geometry without claiming a downstream theorem. This is more than a pointwise kernel evaluation or a gratuitous parameter slice.
